subject: HelioSearch pilot: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + forecasting — next steps
related_links: Jira: SUP-4874 (reference: max too low -> throttling guidance)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@heliosearch.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Hyejin Park <hyejin.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: HelioSearch pilot: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + forecasting — next steps

Hi Asha, Ben —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Wanted to follow up with a crisp summary of what we’re proposing for the Dedicated autoscaling pilot, and what we need from HelioSearch to make the forecasting piece useful.

Summary: Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) behavior
- Min capacity: you configure a floor (min GPUs/replicas). Autoscaler will not scale below this during normal operation.
- Max capacity: you configure a hard cap (max GPUs/replicas). Autoscaler will not scale above this cap. If demand exceeds max, the system will throttle/queue (and you’ll see it clearly in metrics/audit events).
- Burst-to-max (optional): ability to ramp quickly up to max for a burst, then respect cooldowns/scale-down rate limits to avoid oscillation.
- Guardrails/validation: min <= max; bounds must be valid for the region/hardware class; we’ll provide sane defaults for knobs (cooldowns, scale-rate limit) unless you want to override.
- Predictive scaling: we’ll blend reactive signals (queue depth, GPU utilization, p95 latency) with a short-horizon forecast. Forecast is gated by confidence; if confidence is low, autoscaler falls back to reactive-only behavior.
- Transparency: we will provide a scaling decision/audit trail (“why did we scale?”) including clamp reasons (e.g., “clamped_to_max”) and the inputs used.

What we need from HelioSearch (for forecast + sizing)
If you can share either (a) a week of historical traffic, or (b) a representative “expected pattern” for the pilot, we can tune the initial forecast and avoid the classic ramp-up latency spike.

Specifically helpful:
1) Time series shape (hourly is fine)
   - QPS / requests per second by hour (or 5-min if easy)
   - Average + p95 tokens per request (prompt + completion)
   - Any weekday/weekend differences
2) Known scheduled events
   - Re-index jobs, batch runs, cron-like spikes
   - Product launches/promos that create predictable step-changes
3) SLO expectations for the pilot
   - Target p95 latency and whether you care more about TTFT vs end-to-end
   - Any “must not throttle” windows
4) Deployment constraints
   - Preferred region(s)
   - GPU class you’re currently using / want to pin to

I attached a quick one-pager describing the pilot and an XLSX template if that’s easier than exporting raw metrics.

Pilot kickoff scheduling
Can we do a 45-min kickoff next week? Proposed times (PST):
- Tue 1/13 10:00–10:45
- Wed 1/14 1:00–1:45
- Thu 1/15 9:30–10:15

If you reply with the best time + who should attend from your side (SRE/infra owner, app owner), we’ll send an agenda.

Best,
Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- HelioSearch-Pilot-Bounds-and-Forecast-Overview.pdf
- heliosearch-traffic-patterns-template.xlsx

From: Asha Mehta <asha@heliosearch.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Rivera <ben@heliosearch.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 12:06 PM PST
Subject: Re: HelioSearch pilot: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + forecasting — next steps

Hi Lauren,

This is helpful, thank you.

A few clarifying questions:
1) When we hit max, do you queue by default or fail fast? We prefer queuing up to a point and then returning 429s.
2) For min — if there’s a maintenance/drain event, what happens if you can’t keep us at min? (We’ve had issues with “best effort” semantics elsewhere.)
3) How visible is the “clamped_to_max” situation for our oncall? We need something we can page on.

On data: we can share hourly request volumes and tokens/request from our app metrics. I’ll have Ben pull a week of data. Our pattern is pretty stable except for a nightly batch that kicks off at ~01:00 PT.

Kickoff: Wed 1/14 1:00–1:45 PM PT works.

-Asha

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@heliosearch.com>
Cc: Ben Rivera <ben@heliosearch.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Hyejin Park <hyejin.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 1:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: HelioSearch pilot: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + forecasting — next steps

Asha —

Great questions. Answers inline:

1) Hit max: queue vs fail-fast
- Default behavior for Dedicated is queue + apply backpressure, then 429 once queue depth/time exceeds threshold.
- For the pilot we can align the thresholds with your app behavior (e.g., “queue up to N seconds then 429”).

2) Min during maintenance/drain
- Operationally there are rare cases (e.g., regional capacity event / host drain) where maintaining min may require a brief degrade.
- The *config* semantics are: autoscaler won’t choose < min, but the fleet may temporarily be unable to satisfy it. When that happens we emit explicit events/metrics (“min_unavailable”) and prioritize recovery.
- We can walk through the exact behavior and escalation during kickoff; Markus/Hyejin will also cover what knobs we have during an incident (freeze scaling, pin replicas, etc.).

3) Visibility + paging for clamp_to_max
- You’ll have customer-visible indicators in Console + metrics for clamp reasons and throttle/queue impact.
- For the pilot, we’ll also set up a straightforward alert: “clamped_to_max AND sustained queue depth” (i.e., not paging on transient blips).

Data share
Hourly volumes + tokens/request + the nightly batch timing is perfect. If you can include:
- typical batch duration (e.g., 20 min vs 3 hours)
- whether it’s strict-start at 01:00 or drifts
…that materially improves the forecast.

Kickoff confirmed
Locked in Wed 1/14 1:00–1:45 PM PT. Markus (Solutions) and Hyejin (Solutions Eng) are cc’d and will join.

Agenda (proposed):
- Confirm pilot success criteria (latency + spend bounds)
- Confirm min/max + burst behavior you want
- Review traffic pattern + batch job behavior
- Rollout plan (enablement, monitoring, rollback)

Thanks,
Lauren
